claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a closely related HEA derivative has high saturation magnetization and coercivity of approximately 100 Oe or less.
A controlled aging heat treatment can nucleate and grow nanoscale coherent secondary-phase precipitates within an fcc FeCoNi matrix.
An ordered B2 phase is a candidate precipitate for aged fcc FeCoNi.
Composition and annealing conditions can control the length scale of phase decomposition in a high-entropy alloy.
Suitable aging can produce a fine, homogeneous precipitate dispersion without excessive coarsening.
The aging treatment leaves the alloy's overall chemical composition unchanged.
The intended structural mediator is a uniform dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates in the fcc matrix.
The precipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Precipitate pinning inhibits domain-wall motion during magnetization reversal.
Inhibiting domain-wall motion increases coercivity relative to the single-phase material.
Aging-induced precipitation will increase the coercive field to above 100 Oe.
The aged alloy will retain saturation magnetization comparable to that of single-phase fcc FeCoNi or the matched derivative.
In an AlCoFeNi-based HEA, replacing Co with Cr substantially reduces saturation magnetization and increases coercivity.
The proposed comparison is restricted to identical-chemistry aged and single-phase controls measured using the same room-temperature magnetic-field protocol.
TEM or equivalent microstructural characterization can determine whether the intended precipitates formed and measure their size and distribution.
